factors.name: Depth-gated fresh wick asymmetry (absorption imbalance)
factors.description: Per bar computes range-normalised wick asymmetry ((high-max(open,close)) - (min(open,close)-low)) / (high-low), multiplies it by a relative-depth gate (bar volume relative to its 60-bar norm divided by relative bar range), exponentially weights the last few bars (halflife 2), and returns the cross-sectional rank of the negative: rejected, absorbed upside probes score low.
factors.trading_idea: Hidden resting liquidity is identified not by volume alone but by volume traded per unit of price displacement: a bar that absorbs unusually heavy flow while travelling an unusually small range is a bar in which a deep, largely invisible queue sat in the book. Conditioning the bar's failed-excursion asymmetry (upper wick minus lower wick, expressed as a fraction of the bar range, so it is a scale-free shape statistic needing no diffusion-scale estimate) on this Kyle-inverse depth measure isolates probes that were genuinely absorbed rather than mid-quote flicker; the surviving iceberg keeps capping the probed side for the next few bars, so price drifts toward the untested side. Because the effect lives in the residual life of a specific hidden queue, it decays in seconds, so the child weights only the freshest bars (exponential halflife of 2 bars) instead of smearing 18 bars — which is why the parent's edge leaked out to 24 bars and was weak at the fixed 6-bar offset. It persists against arbitrage because the size being inferred is never quoted: exploiting it requires crossing the spread against concealed depth, a cost that quote-only statistical arbitrageurs will not pay. Falsified if depth-gated wick asymmetry carries no more forward sign than raw volume-weighted wick asymmetry, i.e. if the interaction with volume-per-range is flat.

factors.name: Square-root-law weighted flow pressure freshness wedge
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of (sqrt-volume-weighted mean of bar-return signs over the last 6 bars) minus (the same sqrt-volume-weighted mean over the last 60 bars): long names whose newest volume-weighted directional pressure exceeds their already-established pressure.
factors.trading_idea: Under the square-root impact law a bar's contribution to repricing scales with the square root of its executed volume, and under Bouchaud's propagator the impact of volume executed several bars ago is largely transient and relaxes, while flow arriving in the last few bars is mostly unfinished and keeps arriving (order-flow imbalance is strongly autocorrelated at second scales). The child therefore measures a name's sqrt-volume-weighted directional consistency over a fast window matched to the forecast horizon and subtracts the same statistic over a slow window: what remains is *fresh* one-sided pressure net of pressure that has already been impacted and is decaying. This replaces the parent's noisy volume-CV 'metronome' gate (a fragile z-score of a z-score) with a single scale-free statistic that is bounded in [-1,1], robust to single giant prints (sqrt weighting, not linear), and needs no per-name normalisation. Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns do not load positively on fresh-minus-stale sqrt-weighted flow pressure — in particular if the fast and slow components carry the same IC sign — the propagator/unfinished-order interpretation is wrong; the edge survives arbitrage because it lives inside a one-minute window where net-of-spread capacity is tiny and its exploitation does not cancel the child orders still to come.

factors.name: Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of (30-bar signed path-efficiency ratio) x (normalized Shannon entropy of the last 30 bars' volume shares minus its own 120-bar mean): extrapolate the drift when participation just turned unusually even, fade it when volume mass just concentrated into a burst.
factors.trading_idea: A metaorder worked by a scheduler spreads its child fills almost evenly across consecutive 10-second bars, so the *entropy of the bar-volume shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level while price grinds directionally; the unfinished remainder of that parent order makes the grind continue over the next minute. A liquidity-consuming burst or news print does the opposite: volume mass concentrates in one or two bars (entropy drops) and the accompanying displacement is mostly transient impact that decays as depth refills, so the same displacement should be faded. The child keeps the parent's schedule-vs-burst split but expresses both legs with *bounded, scale-free* statistics — normalized Shannon entropy of volume shares (in [0,1]) minus its own trailing mean, times the Kaufman path-efficiency ratio (in [-1,1]) — eliminating the parent's fragile ratio-of-rolling-moments z-scores, clips and tanh that produced the in-sample/out-of-sample collapse. The edge survives arbitrage because detecting a schedule requires per-name conditioning on the *shape* of participation rather than its level, execution algos deliberately randomise size so the residual regularity is small and unrewarding to slow capital, and front-running the remaining children does not eliminate them — each new metaorder regenerates the signal.

factors.name: Rank-drift × increment-compression metaorder wedge
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of (rank-normalised Wilcoxon location shift of the last 6 log-increments versus the trailing 120-bar own-name distribution) × (increment-dispersion compression gate = 1 − 2·rank of the 18-bar variance of uniformized increments minus 1/12): long steady low-dispersion up-drifts, short violent high-dispersion up-moves.
factors.trading_idea: A net price displacement can be produced two ways with opposite futures: (a) by many small, unusually *compressed* increments — the signature of an execution algorithm slicing a large metaorder, which keeps arriving and therefore keeps repricing; or (b) by a few violent increments drawn from the tails of the name's own recent increment distribution — a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot whose impact is largely transient and relaxes as depth refills. The parent measured only the magnitude/direction of fresh pressure, so it loaded mainly on regime (b) and its IC came out negative; the child separates the two regimes with a purely nonparametric two-sample construction: a Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last 6 increments against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution, multiplied by a centred Mood-type *scale-compression* state (rolling variance of the uniformized increments below its uniform benchmark 1/12). The edge survives arbitrage because identifying an in-progress sliced order requires conditioning on the *shape* of the increment distribution rather than the size of the move, and the agent whose child orders create the drift cannot profit from front-running itself; net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is tiny.

factors.name: Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of a blend between (i) the negated, sector-purged, participation-weighted close-location displacement after removing its trailing regression on the shock-identified owed systematic-delivery gap, and (ii) that owed gap itself, routed by the rank of the participation-weighted within-bar wick (absorption) share of the last 6 bars.
factors.trading_idea: Parent B's participation-weighted range-position displacement measures where inside a heavy-volume bar the mid ended up, i.e. the unpaid cost of immediacy that relaxes as depth refills; Parent A's shock-selected distributed-lag kernel measures how much systematic move the name still OWES the market impulse. The child first *purges* the displacement of the part that is mechanically explained by the owed-delivery gap (trailing per-name OLS residual of displacement on the gap), so the fade is applied only to displacement nobody was entitled to, and then routes between the two channels with a state variable neither parent uses: the participation-weighted wick share of the last 6 bars (range minus body over range), which distinguishes bars where aggressive size was absorbed and retraced from clean directional body moves. Where absorption is high the un-owed displacement is pure liquidity provision and snaps back; where bars are body-dominated the displacement is beta delivery in progress and the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign. The interaction is the edge: B cannot tell a low close inside a heavy range from legitimate downside beta delivery, and A has no within-bar geometry to know whether the push was absorbed or accepted.

factors.name: Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback
factors.description: Per bar, cross-sectionally regress returns on the beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity (-log dollar turnover) to extract a mechanical factor return; accumulate it with an exponential kernel gated by a basket-program detector (alignment of dollar-volume-share deviations with the cap-weight vector), and short names in proportion to their orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulated push.
factors.trading_idea: Basket/program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight rather than by fundamental beta, so their price displacement loads on a name's weight-per-unit-depth elasticity kappa = marketCap / dollar-volume, a characteristic that is orthogonal to beta only after explicit projection. Rather than *assuming* the mechanical push equals kappa times the cap-weighted market return (the parent's single common scalar, which makes every cross-sectional bet a static pattern timed by a beta-like market signal), I *measure* it: each bar I run a cross-sectional regression of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity exposure and read off the realised 'mechanical factor return' g_t — the actual displacement per unit of impact elasticity, cleanly separated from the information (beta) channel. Accumulating g_t with an exponential memory only over bars whose cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector (the basket footprint) isolates uncompensated liquidity demand, which must relax; the signal is minus the name's orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulation. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the depth-heterogeneous mechanical component un-hedged, and capturing it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.

factors.name: Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)
factors.description: Piecewise (hinge) interaction between a volatility-scaled 12-bar market-neutral price dislocation and point-in-time corporate net share demand: long the dip in net repurchasers, short the rally in net issuers, with the magnitude scaled by current relative volume and the cross-section demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Firms are the one class of participant whose trading direction is known in advance and is price-insensitive: an active repurchaser has a standing algorithmic *bid* working the tape all day (Rule 10b-18 VWAP slicing), while a net issuer (ATM/secondary/option-driven supply) is a standing *offer*. This makes short-horizon liquidity provision asymmetric at the firm level: an idiosyncratic dip in a heavy repurchaser is absorbed by corporate demand and snaps back within a minute, whereas a rally in a net issuer is capped by corporate supply — so the reversal coefficient should be a hinge in the sign of the dislocation interacted with the sign of net corporate share issuance, not a symmetric linear reversal. Because participation is capped as a fraction of contemporaneous volume, the support strength scales with current relative volume. The edge survives arbitrage because intraday buyback schedules are never disclosed (only quarterly totals), so an arbitrageur cannot distinguish a corporate-supported dip from genuine adverse information ex ante and must warehouse inventory risk; it is falsified if downside reversion at 6 bars is identical for repurchasers and issuers, i.e. if the hinge interaction adds nothing over symmetric reversal.

factors.name: Comparable-basket dislocation with per-name repair rate on a peer-activity clock
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of a per-name 6-bar return forecast: the noise-averaged deviation of log price from its valuation-comparable basket (industry x size-half, leave-one-out) relative to its own 600-bar level, multiplied by a trailing per-name horizon-matched OLS loading (shrunk empirical-Bayes style toward the cross-sectional median loading by fit R-squared) and by a positive repair-capacity gate built from leave-one-out peer activity and the name's rolling correlation with its basket.
factors.trading_idea: A name's deviation from its *valuation-comparable* basket (same industry AND same size half, because dealers hedge inventory with similar-cap same-industry names) is repaired at a speed that differs per name and is proportional to how much hedging capacity is live in that basket right now. The parent measured the dislocation and gated it with coarse 2x2 activity cells but fitted a single pooled loading, so names whose natural repair half-life is far from 60 seconds diluted the 6-bar signal (its IC peaked at 24 bars); the child instead estimates each name's own horizon-matched repair loading by a trailing OLS of the realised 6-bar comparable-relative return on the lagged, noise-averaged dislocation, and scales it by a continuous repair-capacity clock = (peer leave-one-out activity) x (statistical hedge quality of the basket for that name). Falsifiable predictions: (i) names with an empirically fast, well-identified 6-bar repair loading carry essentially all of the 6-bar edge and names with weak/slow loadings carry none; (ii) the same dislocation predicts a strictly smaller repair when its comparables are quiet or poorly correlated with it. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a capacity constraint, not a mispricing: closing an idiosyncratic dislocation consumes hedging capital and simultaneous comparable-basket liquidity, and in the states where that liquidity is absent nobody can force the repair inside a minute.

factors.name: Volatility-matched round-number lattice barrier asymmetry
factors.description: Chooses per name the round-price grid (0.05…1.00) whose spacing best matches ~2x the trailing dollar sigma of 6-bar moves, then scores -sign(recent drift) x [exp(-distance to the node ahead / sigma) - exp(-distance to the node behind / sigma)], amplified by the name's measured excess occupancy of node neighbourhoods, ranked cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: Human limit-order placement clusters on round price nodes (…x.00, x.50, x.25, x.10, x.05), so the book carries excess resting depth exactly at those levels; the relevant node spacing is the one comparable to the distance price actually travels over the forecast horizon. A mid drifting *into* the nearest node therefore meets an abnormally thick wall and stalls/retreats, while a mid that has just *passed* a node has consumed that depth and faces a thinner book on the far side, so it continues. The child expresses this as a single antisymmetric function of the price's position inside its volatility-matched lattice cell, signed by the direction of travel — so it is resistance and post-breach continuation in one term whose time-series mean loading on plain reversal is ~zero (position within a cell is nearly uniform), which is why it is not another reversal clone. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick, it lives in the price *level modulo a lattice* — a non-scale-invariant feature that virtually every return-based model normalises away — and crossing the spread to harvest it costs more than the drift for anyone not already resting in the queue.

factors.name: Kalman-gain transient deviation with noise-purged path memory
factors.description: Signal = (−(log-price minus per-name Kalman-gain EWMA of the idiosyncratic log-price path) + ρ_eff × filtered 6-bar efficient displacement) / 6-bar efficient volatility, where the noise variance, Hurst exponent and Kalman gain come from a three-scale (1/4/16-bar) mean-absolute-displacement decomposition; cross-sectionally median-demeaned each bar.
factors.trading_idea: Observed mid = efficient price + a transient deviation (quote bounce, discreteness, unwinding impact); over a 60-second horizon the *only* reliably forecastable part of the observed mid change is the reversal of that deviation, which is exactly the term the parent subtracted out — hence its declared sign was contradicted. This child identifies the noise variance exactly (invariantly to how rough the efficient price is) from mean-absolute displacements at three geometrically spaced scales (1/4/16 bars), since Var(D_k)=A·k^(2H)+2σ²_ε implies the closed form 2σ²_ε=(V₄²−V₁V₁₆)/(2V₄−V₁−V₁₆); the resulting noise-to-signal ratio q fixes each name's steady-state local-level Kalman gain K=(√(q²+4q)−q)/2, so the transient deviation is measured as the price minus a per-name-bandwidth EWMA rather than a common-lookback deviation. The forecast is −ε̂ (fade the estimated transient) plus the fractional-Gaussian block memory ρ=2^(2H−1)−1 applied to the *filtered* efficient displacement (follow genuinely persistent efficient paths), all in units of the name's 6-bar efficient volatility. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common filter bandwidth and one common reversion coefficient to the whole book: the residual is the cross-sectional dispersion of the optimal bandwidth and of the noise-purged roughness, worth only a few basis points per name and requiring continuous per-name re-estimation.

factors.name: Churn-resilience gated sweep-impact snapback
factors.description: Participation- and purity-weighted close-location displacement over the last 6 bars (impact debt from directional sweep bars), sector-demeaned, multiplied by a cross-sectional rank of the name's lagged volume-weighted intrabar churn (book resilience / replenishment speed), sign-flipped and cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Transient impact is only repaid when the opposite side of the book replenishes, so the *speed* of the snapback — not its existence — is what decides whether it lands inside a fixed 60-second window. Two observable quantities separate the two halves of that statement: bar-level directional purity |close-open|/range identifies which bars actually spent volume walking the book (a sweep creates impact debt, a two-sided churn bar does not), while a name's ambient volume-weighted churn over the preceding few minutes (traded participation that produces little net displacement) measures how fast its book two-sides and therefore how much of the debt is repaid per unit of clock time. The parent mixed fast- and slow-replenishing names, which is exactly why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars; tilting the same idiosyncratic, participation-weighted range-position displacement toward high-churn (high-resilience) names moves the mass of the repayment into the fixed 6-bar horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires posting passive size against impatient aggressors in exactly the depth that generated the displacement, so capacity is capped by the illiquidity that creates the signal; falsifiable if the 6-bar reversion of sweep debt is independent of (or decreasing in) the lagged churn-resilience measure.

factors.name: Rice-consistency wedge gated crossing-clock fade
factors.description: Negative trailing-standardised idiosyncratic price deviation, weighted by the sech^2 clock-match kernel built from the mean spacing between its zero crossings, and gated by a logistic function of the wedge between the observed 6-bar block sign-concordance autocorrelation (Rice-inverted) and the value implied by the crossing-clock AR(1) persistence; cross-sectionally ranked and demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: Both parents estimate a per-name reversion timescale from *sign* statistics, but on different objects: Parent A counts zero-crossings of the price deviation (Rice inversion on the LEVEL, giving an implied AR(1) persistence phi = cos(pi/T)), while Parent B inverts Rice on the 6-bar INCREMENTS (rho_obs = cos(pi*p_flip)). Under a stationary OU/AR(1) level these two are analytically linked — the lag-h block-increment autocorrelation must equal rho_pred = -(1 - phi^h)/2 — so the wedge rho_obs - rho_pred (shrunk by the number of independent block pairs) is a model-free measure of directional persistence in excess of what the name's own crossing clock can generate, i.e. evidence that the deviation is being carried by transient order-flow/stale-quote lag rather than by a stationary oscillation. Parent B's realized sign (concordant displacements *revert*) says exactly this excess concordance is transient impact awaiting unwind, so the child fades Parent A's horizon-matched deviation with a gate that opens where the wedge is positive and closes where the observed block memory is already OU-consistent (nothing left to harvest at 6 bars). Neither parent has this: A ignores whether the deviation is stationary oscillation or live push, and B misreads its own rho as a forecast coefficient instead of as a departure from the level-implied benchmark.

factors.name: Block-run surprisal versus per-name flip baseline
factors.description: For each name, the contiguous run length L and cumulative standardised displacement D of adjacent non-overlapping 6-bar blocks are computed, the run's surprisal (L-1)·(-ln(1-p_flip)) is evaluated against a purged trailing estimate of the name's own block sign-flip frequency, and the signal is minus the bounded run displacement times that surprisal, cross-sectionally median-demeaned.
factors.trading_idea: The parent's durable asset was the scale-free, jump-robust sign statistic p_flip — the frequency with which a name's adjacent 6-bar displacements change sign — but it used that statistic *in-sample*, so a name in the middle of a directional run mechanically got a high estimated continuation coefficient and the factor ended up buying long runs; the realized negative IC says those runs are exactly what reverts, which is why the declared direction was contradicted. The child keeps the per-name sign statistic but reverses its role: p_flip, estimated on a window purged of the current run, defines a per-name geometric null for how long same-signed 60-second displacements should persist, and the *surprisal* of the observed contiguous run, (L-1)·(-ln(1-p_flip)), measures how much of the run cannot be explained by the name's own memory. Excess persistence of that kind is produced by an exogenous, finite liquidity demand (a sliced metaorder or a withdrawn liquidity provider), and finite demand terminates: the un-owed part of the displacement is transient impact that relaxes over the next minute, so the child forecasts reversal in proportion to run surprisal times the standardised cumulative run displacement. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common reversion speed to the whole cross-section, whereas the tradable residual is the per-name *calibration* of what counts as surprising persistence — it requires continuous re-estimation of p_flip per name, pays a few basis points per name, and only becomes economic when diversified across a broad book.

factors.name: Program-flow vs name-flow volume split: conditional reversal flip
factors.description: Cross-sectional rank of minus (3-bar idiosyncratic return z-score) times a signed weight tanh(common volume surprise − idiosyncratic volume surprise), where the volume surprise is split by a trailing beta on the panel-wide volume surprise and the weight is cross-sectionally demeaned so the signal is the interaction, not a repackaged reversal factor.
factors.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution a large share of traded volume is mechanical, market-wide flow (index/ETF arbitrage, basket and program trades) that consumes depth in every name simultaneously without carrying any name-specific information, while the remainder is name-specific flow that is far more likely to be informed and order-split. The classic volume-conditioned reversal treats all volume alike; the child instead decomposes each name's contemporaneous log-volume surprise into a common part (its trailing beta on the panel-wide volume surprise) and an idiosyncratic residual, and uses the *sign of that split* to flip the direction in which the last 30 seconds of idiosyncratic price move is traded: fade moves whose volume was common-driven (pure depth consumption, mean-reverting transient impact), follow moves whose volume was name-specific (informed, mechanically persistent metaorder flow). Falsifiable: reversal IC at 6 bars should be strongly positive in the common-volume half of the panel and zero-or-negative (continuation) in the name-volume half; if reversal strength is invariant to the split, the mechanism is dead. The edge survives arbitrage because separating program flow from informed flow in real time requires a cross-sectional volume-commonality estimate that a single-name liquidity provider does not compute, and the payoff is a fraction of the spread earned as compensation for supplying depth against recurring mechanical flow.

factors.name: Volume-at-level wall vs vacuum idiosyncratic dislocation flip
factors.description: Volume-standardised idiosyncratic (market-beta-residual) decay-weighted 4-bar dislocation, cross-sectionally z-scored, multiplied by minus a doubly-centred tanh gate on the volume-weighted local-time density of the mid at its current level, and weighted by an onset factor that keeps dislocations at their own 8-bar extreme.
factors.trading_idea: The parent measured occupancy of the mid at its CURRENT (post-move) level and then assumed that occupancy described depth already consumed — hence its continuation prediction; the realized IC was negative on both legs, which is exactly what you get if occupancy instead describes the resting/latent liquidity standing AHEAD of the displaced price. I keep the parent's peer-orthogonal dislocation and its doubly-centred occupancy gate but re-read the state variable correctly and upgrade it from a bar-count local time to a volume-weighted local time (latent depth accumulates in proportion to volume transacted at a level, Bouchaud's latent-liquidity/market-profile picture), so a whitened idiosyncratic displacement into a heavily-traded level meets a replenishing wall and is absorbed back inside seconds, whereas the same displacement into a level the tape has barely visited meets a vacuum, forcing market makers to re-quote around the new level, and the move persists. To place the response inside the fixed 6-bar offset (the parent's |IC| leaked out to 24 bars because both its dislocation and its state were slow), the dislocation is shortened and decay-weighted, the occupancy window and its time z-score are shortened, and the signal is scaled by an onset weight that keeps only names whose dislocation is at its own 8-bar extreme right now — absorption and re-quoting both resolve immediately after the displacement completes. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a conditional sign flip: unconditionally (gate centred in time and cross-section) the factor has zero loading on reversal or momentum, so it is invisible to standard screens, and exploiting it requires paying the spread at exactly the levels where depth is thinnest.

factors.name: Reignition-hazard gated pending silence displacement vs paid impact
factors.description: Cross-sectionally standardised pending vol-scaled displacement of the current silence spell (sum of returns since the last traded bar / sqrt(spell length)), weighted by tanh of the cross-sectionally standardised 6-bar reignition probability, minus a decay-weighted 6-bar traded-bar displacement weighted by the same arrival-rate state.
factors.trading_idea: The parent proved that quote-driven (thin-volume) mid drift continues while volume-paid drift decays, but it pooled the quiet leg over a 12-bar decay window, turning it into a slow state variable whose IC only peaked at 12 bars. The child measures the object that actually resolves inside the forecast horizon: the *pending* displacement accumulated over the current, still-unbroken silence spell (cumulative vol-scaled return since the last volume-bearing bar, scaled by sqrt of spell length) — this is exactly the repricing that the next arriving order must validate or erase. It is gated by a horizon-matched reignition probability p = 1-(1-lambda)^6, where lambda is the name's recent trade-bar frequency, standardised cross-sectionally so a market-wide lull is purged: a name likely to be hit within the next 6 bars has its pending quiet drift confirmed (continuation), while a name whose expected silence exceeds the horizon is showing stale-quote flicker that mean-reverts, and a busy name is mostly carrying transient impact that decays. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in names that are, at that instant, quiet and thinly quoted; it is falsified if pending-spell displacement predicts forward returns independently of the 6-bar reignition probability, or if the paid leg does not revert more strongly in high-arrival-rate names.

factors.name: Trade-backing split bivariate VAR with 6-bar window-mass gate
factors.description: Per-name trailing Yule-Walker VAR(1) on the trade-backed / unbacked multiplicative split of the cross-sectionally demeaned return, ridged and shrunk toward the pooled system, projected 6 steps via the summed companion powers and scaled by the eigenvalue-implied in-window response mass (1 - rho^6), then ranked cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: Each bar's idiosyncratic move splits multiplicatively into a trade-backed leg (return x trailing volume percentile) and an unbacked quote-drift leg (return x one minus that percentile): only the backed leg transfers inventory and therefore creates a repayment obligation, while unbacked drift is pure quote relocation that must either be confirmed by later aggressive flow or snap back. Because the two legs feed each other — absorbed pushes provoke quote relocation, and unbacked drift attracts flow that validates or refutes it — the expected return over exactly the next 6 bars is the 6-step summed impulse response of the *bivariate* system, not the mass of a single-equation body->seam lag kernel; cross-channel feedback makes the intermediate-horizon response hump-shaped or sign-flipped, which is precisely why the parent's single-equation kernel leaked its power to 12 bars. So we fit a 2x2 VAR(1) per name by trailing ridged Yule-Walker, shrink it toward the pooled cross-sectional system, iterate the companion matrix six steps, and gate the forecast by the eigenvalue-implied fraction of total response mass that lands inside the window, 1 - rho^6, shrinking out names whose repayment is too slow to complete by t+6. The edge survives arbitrage because collecting it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggression for a fraction of the spread (inventory risk that cannot be lifted directionally), and because the per-name coefficients and the backing split are re-estimated continuously rather than imposed.

factors.name: Delivery-capped flow-attributed valuation repair
factors.description: Attributes the 6-bar change in a name's industry-demeaned log valuation multiple to idiosyncratic-flow impact, basket-flow impact and an unbacked quiet residual; scores +idio·(forecast volume rate) minus the transitory part after weighting it by the expected in-window delivery share and clipping its magnitude to the Kyle-lambda × forecast-6-bar-volume repair capacity, with the fade scaled by leave-one-out peer activity and valuation-anchor overshoot concordance.
factors.trading_idea: Parent B says the transitory (basket-flow-pushed plus flow-unbacked 'quiet') part of a name's industry-demeaned valuation-multiple dislocation is what snaps back, while Parent A says how much of any owed push actually resolves is set by business time — the volume the next six bars are forecast to trade. The child fuses them non-additively: the transitory dislocation is first re-weighted by Parent A's still-owed × deliverable share (min(owed volume-clock weight, Hawkes-style forecast volume rate)) and then HARD-CLIPPED to the maximum price move six bars of forecast flow can physically produce, cap = lambda · 6 · E[|f|] · directional-efficiency, expressed in the same trailing return-sd units as the dislocation itself. The interaction is the edge: Parent B fades dislocations that are too large to be repaired inside the fixed 6-bar offset (hence its IC keeps growing to 24 bars), and Parent A shrinks its whole leg differential with no idea of where the snap-back target is or how big the repair must be — only the clip of a valuation-anchored repair distance by a Kyle-lambda × forecast-volume capacity gives a signal whose realizable component is matched to exactly six bars, while the informed idiosyncratic-flow leg is followed with a forecast-rate (not owed-capped) weight because continuation needs fresh flow, not worked-off flow.
